overall: The AG found the Dartmouth Select Board violated the Open Meeting Law by posting notice of its December 16, 2020 emergency meeting less than 48 hours in advance; the other two allegations were withdrawn. Ordered future compliance only, with a caution about intent.

allegations.summary: Board posted notice of a December 16, 2020 meeting less than 48 hours ahead, calling it an emergency to appoint an alternate building commissioner after a last-minute resignation.
allegations.key_passage: We are not persuaded that the unexpected resignation of the alternate building commissioner constituted an “emergency” as defined by the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the remote-access link stopped working after the meeting adjourned. The complainant withdrew this allegation.
allegations.key_passage: We note that, even if true, this allegation would not constitute a violation of G.L. c. 30A, §§ 18-25.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Board failed to announce the name of each member participating remotely. The complainant withdrew this allegation.
allegations.key_passage: Mr. Higgins has since withdrawn this allegation after we addressed a similar issue, and found no violation, in OML 2020-168.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law
remedy_passage: We order the Board’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
